messages:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert auto-post: Incident PD-8342 triggered for region-eu-west-2 network_probe_failures (severity: high) :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Alert summary: multiple synthetic probes failing in eu-west-2 starting ~1762345600, 30%+ probe failures to our edge endpoints, possible cross-AZ routing anomalies.

Alex R: I’m on it. Paging @Mira S and @NetworkOps.

Mira S: Got it. Looking at dashboard — synthetic check spike aligned with a bunch of 5xx/timeout from our health-check agents.

Sam T: I can confirm from the HTTP probe logs: timeouts from probes in AZ-a and AZ-b, but AZ-c looks okay. Could be a routing flap between AZs.

Jules P: PD page details show repeated retries from our global-probes fleet. Not seeing corresponding increase in customer 5xx in app metrics yet, curious if probes are lying.

NetworkOps: We’re checking the backbone peering metrics with provider. Initial telemetry: slight packet loss on a subset of links in eu-west-2, BGP withdraws visible ~1762345550-1762345650.

Alex R: Ok — we need to confirm two things: 1) Are these false positives (probe-only) or real customer impact? 2) If real, mitigations (reroute, scale, failover).

Mira S: Quick check: internal service latency SLOs show minor noise but not a widespread error increase. A small cohort of customers in eu-west shows elevated tail latency.

Sam T: Reproducing probe from my laptop -> `curl -v https://edge-eu-west-2.redwood.example/health` -> sometimes hangs at TCP connect stage.

Sam T: Pasting quick run:```
$ curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://edge-eu-west-2.redwood.example/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://edge-eu-west-2.redwood.example/health
* Connected to edge-eu-west-2.redwood.example (52.95.x.x) port 443 (#0)
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connection timed out after 5001 milliseconds
```

Jules P: That aligns with the probe timeouts. Cloud provider console shows intermittent route table flaps in eu-west-2b.

oncall-bot: Automated runbook suggestion: `Runbook -> Regional Network Probe Failures` (link: https://redwood.runbooks.example/regional-probes). Suggested steps: disable synthetic checks, gather packet captures, open provider ticket, escalate to SE.

Alex R: I’m going to disable synthetic probes for eu-west-2 to stop noisy alerts and reduce alert churn — will annotate PD.

Mira S: +1. If probes are causing noise it masks real signals. Also enable higher-fidelity telemetry on real customer traffic.

Sam T: Executing: `./ops/synthetics disable --region eu-west-2 --reason \"investigating probe flapping\"`

Sam T: Done. Noted on PD. @pagerduty-bot update: muted synthetic check alerts for eu-west-2.

pagerduty-bot: Update recorded on PD-8342: synthetic checks muted for eu-west-2 by Sam T.

NetworkOps: Provider case opened (case 789321). They acknowledge intermittent reaching blackholes between AZ-a and AZ-b. Asking for packet captures and timestamps.

Jules P: Collecting tcptrace/pcaps from edge nodes. Command: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/euw2_probe.pcap host 52.95.x.x and port 443` running on edge instances. Will share S3 link when uploaded.

Mira S: Noted that our internal fallback routing (cross-AZ) didn't kick for some prefixes due to a stale route-policy. I’m applying a temporary policy to prefer healthy paths as a mitigation.

Alex R: Good — are we able to shift customer traffic to other regions for affected customers? What about PCI/data residency?

NetworkOps: We can failover non-residency customers to eu-west-1, but that requires ACL updates and might add latency. For customers in strict regions we’ll keep them and monitor.

Sam T: Meanwhile, add an annotation to internal dashboard: `probe_muted=true` so dashboards don't get false-regression alerts.

Mira S: Also starting a short-lived smoke test against backend services using production-like traffic to verify real user impact.

Mira S: Smoke results: 98% OK, 2% elevated tail latency for a small subset — consistent with earlier note.

Alex R: Communication: drafting status note for affected customers and internal exec. Will post a brief status in #general and #support: \"We are investigating intermittent network connectivity in eu-west-2; synthetic probes muted while we gather provider logs; small cohort of customers may see elevated latency.\"

Jules P: Uploaded pcap to S3: s3://redwood-ops/euw2/pcaps/euw2_probe_1762345820.pcap (provider case ref included).

NetworkOps: Provider responded — they pushed a corrective route update at ~1762345900 and report stabilization. They asked us to re-enable probes to verify.

Sam T: Re-enabling probes now: `./ops/synthetics enable --region eu-west-2`

Sam T: Re-enabled. Monitoring probes.

oncall-bot: Probe check results (1m): 99.7% success for eu-west-2.

Alex R: Looks like flap resolved, leaving PD open until 1h stable. Annotating runbook with provider case id and action taken.

Mira S: Follow-up actions: 1) Add BGP convergence test to synthetic suite to detect partial-route blackholes earlier. 2) Fix stale route-policy causing failed fallback. 3) Improve mapping between synthetic probes and real-customer telemetry so we can quickly classify false positives.

Alex R: Handing off on-call to @Jules P for 1h watch and PD ownership.

Jules P: Took ownership — will monitor and contact provider if we see any regression.

NetworkOps: Closing provider case on our side if stable for 30m, will update PD then.

oncall-bot: Incident PD-8342 status: acknowledged -> monitoring. Last update timestamp 1762345984.

Mira S: Thanks everyone. Postmortem draft will go into /incidents/PD-8342 after stabilization.

Alex R: Great job. :thumbsup:
